title: When the Sigil Falls Again
premise: Silas Nystrom, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent his life in the Hollow Valley, where magic cannot follow and where he fled to bury his past. When a prophecy written a century ago names tonight's date, Silas and the ragtag found family sheltering with him are pulled into a war they never chose: the young King Aldric is being consumed by the Vessel, an ancient sigil-thing wearing his crown. To save him, Silas must reclaim the swordspeech he swore away, knowing each word spoken in power erases one of his own memories. In the end, Silas unbinds the king at the cost of forgetting the family that made him want to survive — but they choose to become his memory, staying beside him as he begins again.
about_author: Mara Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who bargain with what they cannot afford to lose.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet the Hollow Valley's stubborn peace: Silas mends fences, teaches knife-work to runaway Wren, and shares supper with ex-soldier Brannoc and healer Ivetta. He refuses to speak of the scarred words on his forearms. Emotional beat: quiet belonging built on deliberate silence — and the first tremor when the valley's anti-magic hum stutters for the first time in decades.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers a century-old prophecy book in the chapel ruins; tonight's date is inked in fresh ash-black letters. When she reads it aloud, the valley's ward shatters and the five are dragged through a collapsing gate into the capital of Vaelmoor. Emotional beat: terror and wonder colliding as Wren realizes her curiosity has consequences she can't undo.

chapters.title: The City Under the Crown
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The city is beautiful and wrong — citizens smile too widely, guards move like puppets. Brannoc recognizes military discipline turned to servitude. The group is nearly caught by crown-sworn soldiers; a beggar named Osla hides them, hinting the king hasn't been seen truly awake in months. Emotional beat: Brannoc's soldier instincts warring with his vow never to serve again.

chapters.title: What the Swordspeaker Buried
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. Ivetta tends Silas after a skirmish and sees the oath-scars: he bound his swordspeech to escape a massacre he caused. She confronts him gently; he admits the Vessel was born from a broken sigil he helped seal a century of stories ago — no, a lifetime ago he doesn't fully remember. Emotional beat: shame met with compassion, the first crack in his isolation.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Using Osla's smuggler routes, they reach the throne room. King Aldric surfaces briefly behind the Vessel's control and begs — in a child's handwriting of light — for someone to unbind him. Guards attack; Silas speaks one word of swordspeech to save Wren, and forgets his mother's face. Emotional beat: the price made flesh; survival now has a visible cost.

chapters.title: The Cartography of Memory
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren theorizes the prophecy book maps not events but memories — the Vessel feeds on forgotten things. The group raids the royal archive, discovering Silas's name in records a hundred years old. He cannot be twenty-nine. Emotional beat: vertigo and betrayal-tinged confusion as the family realizes Silas has been lying about more than his scars.

chapters.title: Oathbreaker's Confession
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confesses: he sealed the original sigil a century past, paying with his years and memories, then hid in the magicless valley to avoid ever speaking again. The Vessel has been hunting its last unbroken seal — him. The family's anger fractures the group; Wren walks out into the occupied city alone. Emotional beat: found family tested by the weight of what survival has already cost.

chapters.title: The Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, captured. Taken to the palace, Wren is brought before the Vessel, which wears Aldric's body and speaks in Silas's old voice. It offers her a bargain: Silas's forgotten memories, preserved in the sigil, if she delivers him. Wren pretends to accept while stealing a shard of the binding. Emotional beat: courage sharpened by love — choosing loyalty over certainty.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converge on the coronation spire. Silas speaks the full unbinding — surrendering every remaining memory of his family — while Brannoc holds the line, Ivetta anchors Aldric's fading mind, and Wren drives the stolen shard home. The Vessel unravels screaming; Aldric wakes, weeping and free. Emotional beat: triumphant sacrifice, each member giving exactly what they feared most.

chapters.title: Where the Story Keeps Us
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. Silas survives but remembers none of them — a stranger with their scars' history written on his arms. Instead of leaving, they stay: Wren reads him the prophecy book, Brannoc retells their battles, Ivetta keeps his new journal. Aldric offers Silas a place rebuilding Vaelmoor. Emotional beat: bittersweet grace — memory lost, but family chosen twice, and this time written down so it can't be taken.
